correctness.rationale: Under lax splitting the two downward-closed witnesses can be made disjoint. The first side selects at most one y per x, and moving all matching rows there cannot create a violation on either side. Satisfiability is therefore exactly the existence of a selection that leaves at most one z-value per y unselected. An unmixed fibre is irrelevant, and four mixed fibres already give a failing subteam by taking one row of each output from each: the three x-values cannot cover the four fibres. Thus every minimal failure has at most four used fibres, and if four then exactly eight rows. The independently reproduced finite census exhausts multisets of the 49 mixed Boolean states (49, 1225, 20825, 270725 candidates), up to renaming only y. It confirmed the size distributions: k=1 empty; k=2 {4:3,6:6,7:12}; k=3 {6:36,7:12,8:102}; k=4 {8:135}. Testing all single deletions is sufficient by downward closure; explicit witnesses of each allowed size were separately verified by direct split enumeration. Zero or one mixed fibre cannot fail. This proves the spectrum, the count 306 and sharpness of eight for unbounded finite Y.
residual_risks: Finite exact verification is not a formal proof artifact. The theorem depends on set semantics, only the three displayed coordinates, at most three x-values, and Boolean z; no claim is made for larger alphabets or additional attributes.

value.rationale: The chained functional-dependency split is a canonical incoherent two-atom formula; the ternary/Boolean promise is a natural finite-domain step beyond the sharp binary-determinant theorem. Eight is an explicit sharp local witness bound independent of the intermediate-domain size, and the complete catalogue gives usable obstruction information beyond a decision procedure or a nonsharp bound, including the unexpected exclusion of size five and the emergence of sizes seven and eight.
residual_risks: No general formula for larger domains is established; the value is the sharp bounded-domain theorem and exact catalogue.
